title: Finite free transport of regular quotient completion units
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a map of commutative ring sheaves on a small site. Fix an $R$-module basis isomorphism $R^{\oplus d}\cong S$, $d\geq0$, and a global section $a$ of $R$ whose multiplication on both $R$ and $S$ is injective. Assume countable products in both module-sheaf categories are exact. For a K-flat complex $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms over $R$ (tensoring with each term is exact), put $Q=P\otimes_R S$, which computes derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For $T=R,S$ and $H=P,Q$ respectively, let $C_{T,a}(H)$ be the product cone of $H\otimes_T T/a^nT$ with its zero shifted-component quotient unit $\eta_{T,a,H}$ [lem-pur-regular-quotient-completion-unit]. Restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] identifies $Q$ with $P^{\oplus d}$, identifies $C_{S,a}(Q)$ with $C_{R,a}(P)^{\oplus d}$, and under these identifications sends $\eta_{S,a,Q}$ to $\eta_{R,a,P}^{\oplus d}$. Consequently, if $P$ is locally derived $(a)$-complete in the local derived-Hom sense of [lem-pur-regular-quotient-completion-unit], then $Q$ is locally derived $(a)$-complete as an $S$-object. All tensor products of module sheaves are sheafified tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], applied termwise to complexes when an ordinary tensor is written.

source.place: Lemma 3.4.12, pp. 22-23; finite direct-sum calculation of the quotient-tower units, written here as a general ringed-site argument.

proof.text: Write $U$ for restriction from $S$ to $R$. By the module-sheaf limits and colimits theorem, kernels, cokernels and products have the same underlying abelian sheaves for either coefficient ring. Thus $U$ is exact, preserves products and finite sums, and commutes with cohomology. It reflects zero cohomology sheaves because it leaves the underlying abelian sheaf unchanged. Consequently a chain map of $S$-modules is a quasi-isomorphism if its restriction is one. The theorem applies on this small site, where abelian sheafification exists; there is no need to assume enough points.

source.place: Tags 03DA (lemma-abelian) and 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits): exact forgetful functor and underlying limits/colimits.

proof.text:
Let $b_i$ ($1\leq i\leq d$) be the images of the standard basis under the given isomorphism, and let $\lambda_i:S\to R$ be its inverse coordinates. In every cochain degree the maps
$$p\otimes s\longmapsto(\lambda_i(s)p)_i,\qquad (p_i)_i\longmapsto\sum_i p_i\otimes b_i$$
are inverse $R$-linear maps $U(Q)\rightleftarrows P^{\oplus d}$. The forward formula is balanced since $\lambda_i(rs)=r\lambda_i(s)$; the inverse identities follow from $s=\sum_i\lambda_i(s)b_i$ and $\lambda_i(b_j)=\delta_{ij}$. These restriction-compatible formulas extend uniquely through sheafification. They commute with differentials since the $b_i$ and $\lambda_i$ are fixed coefficient maps. Denote this chain isomorphism by $\alpha$. The empty sum gives the same conclusion for $d=0$.

source.place: Section 03EK (section-tensor-product), sheafified sectionwise tensor; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), universal property. Explicit basis calculation.

proof.text:
For any module sheaf $M$ over $T=R$ or $S$, the maps $m\otimes\bar t\mapsto tm\bmod a^nM$ and $m\bmod a^nM\mapsto m\otimes1$ identify $M\otimes_T T/a^nT$ with $M/a^nM$. Balancing makes both well-defined and gives the inverse identities. These are maps of sheaves: quotient sections have lifts locally, the formulas are independent of lifts, and the sheafification universal property glues them. This uses the cited theorem's sheafified-cokernel description, not surjectivity on sections. Since $\alpha(a^n q)=a^n\alpha(q)$, it induces chain isomorphisms
$$\theta_n:U(Q\otimes_S S/a^nS)\xrightarrow{\sim}(P\otimes_R R/a^nR)^{\oplus d}.$$
For $s=\sum_i r_i b_i$ their formula is $\theta_n((p\otimes s)\otimes\bar z)=(p\otimes\overline{\lambda_i(sz)})_i$, where $z$ is any local lift in $S$. Changing $z$ by $a^n w$ changes each coordinate by an $a^n$-multiple. Thus the formula is independent of that lift.

source.place: Tags 03DA (lemma-abelian), 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules) and Section 03EK: quotient sheaves and balanced tensor calculation.

proof.text: Put $V_n=P\otimes_R R/a^nR$ and $W_n=Q\otimes_S S/a^nS$. The quotient transitions in these towers are reduction modulo the lower power. Reducing $\lambda_i(sz)$ modulo $a^n$ after reducing modulo $a^{n+1}$ gives exactly the same coordinate as reducing it directly modulo $a^n$. Hence $\theta_n$ intertwines every tower transition. Products are computed sectionwise, and finite sums equal finite products; the mutually inverse reindexings $((x_{n,i})_i)_n\rightleftarrows((x_{n,i})_n)_i$ identify $\prod_n V_n^{\oplus d}$ with $(\prod_n V_n)^{\oplus d}$. They intertwine $s$, since its $n$-th coordinate is the transition applied to $x_{n+1,i}$, and therefore intertwine $1-s$. Apply this reindexing and $\prod_n\theta_n$ to both product blocks of the shifted cone. Each block map commutes with its differential and with $1-s$, so it commutes with the signed cone differential and its shift. This gives a chain isomorphism $\beta:U(C_{S,a}(Q))\cong C_{R,a}(P)^{\oplus d}$, using exactly the cone model in the cited completion-unit statement.

source.place: Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits): sectionwise products; the two-block cone calculation uses the model of lem-pur-regular-quotient-completion-unit.

proof.text:
For every local $q\in Q$, its image under the specified unit is $((q\otimes1)_n,0)$ in the two product blocks. The quotient calculation gives $\theta_n(q\otimes1)=(\alpha_i(q)\otimes1)_i$. The cone comparison acts separately on its two blocks and therefore carries the zero shifted-product component to zero. Consequently
$$\beta\,U(\eta_{S,a,Q})=(\eta_{R,a,P})^{\oplus d}\alpha$$
as chain maps, not merely as maps to the unshifted product. The formulas also show that the identifications commute with every chain map in $P$.

source.place: Lemma 3.4.12, pp. 22-23, natural completion map; explicit quotient and zero-component refinement from the cited regular quotient unit statement.

proof.text: Suppose $P$ is locally derived $(a)$-complete as in the hypothesis. Apply the regular quotient completion-unit criterion with coefficient ring $R$: $P$ is K-flat, multiplication by $a$ on $R$ is injective, and countable products of $R$-modules are exact, exactly as required. It makes $\eta_{R,a,P}$ an isomorphism in $D(R)$, hence a quasi-isomorphism of the displayed complexes. A finite direct sum of this map is a quasi-isomorphism: kernels and images of its differentials are the coordinatewise finite sums, so its $k$-th cohomology map is $H^k(\eta_{R,a,P})^{\oplus d}$. The identity in step 5 and the chain isomorphisms $\alpha,\beta$ make $U(\eta_{S,a,Q})$ a quasi-isomorphism. Step 1 then makes $\eta_{S,a,Q}$ a quasi-isomorphism over $S$. This includes $d=0$, where both complexes are zero.

source.place: Lemma 3.4.12, natural-map criterion, instantiated by lem-pur-regular-quotient-completion-unit; finite coordinatewise cohomology calculation.

proof.text: Apply K-flat change of rings to $P$ and $R\to S$. Its hypotheses hold because $P$ is K-flat with flat terms; thus $Q$ is K-flat over $S$ with flat terms. Derived change of rings also identifies this $Q$ with $P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$. Now apply the regular quotient completion-unit criterion over $S$: multiplication by the image of $a$ is injective and countable products of $S$-module sheaves are exact by hypothesis, and step 6 supplies its specified invertible unit. Its equivalence gives local derived $(a)$-completeness of $Q$ as an $S$-object, including the required internal-Hom vanishing on every slice for every local section in $(a)S$. This last use of the criterion avoids assuming that an arbitrary local element of $(a)S$ is the image of an element of $R$.

The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged from the base. The item is not dropped, not superseded and has no repair note. It gives exactly what parent lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison step 4 cites, under the hypotheses the parent supplies. Steps: (1) restriction is exact, preserves products and reflects zero cohomology, from clauses (1)-(3) of lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful; this is a declared sk-thm-reduction tool use, and I accept it as generic infrastructure because the unit cites no units and no unit node gives it. (2) The basis coordinates alpha: U(Q)=P^d are correct; I checked balancing via lambda_i(rs)=r lambda_i(s) and the inverse identities. (3) M⊗T/a^n=M/a^nM through local lifts and sheafification; I checked the theta_n formula and that it does not depend on the lift. (4) The transitions, the product reindexing and the same block map on both cone blocks give a chain iso beta. (5) beta U(eta_S)=eta_R^{⊕d} alpha holds as chain maps, with the zero block going to zero. (6) Over R the criterion holds (P K-flat, a regular, products exact); a finite sum of quasi-isos is a quasi-iso, and step 1 reflects it. (7) Q is K-flat with flat terms by lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings; the criterion over S then gives local completeness for every f in (a)S without lifting f to R. Edge cases tested: d=0 (S=0), d=1, P=0, a a unit. No added hypotheses.
